newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA T-BILL RATES LOWER AFTER AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: MANILA T-BILL RATES LOWER AFTER AUCTION.

text.p: Philippine banks quoted lower bid and offer rates in the secondary market on Tuesday in reaction to the fall in rates at the auction, traders said.
The market was swamped with buyers of bills, with the one-year maturity the favourite among banks, because of the view that interest rates are now on a downtrend.
"But we're a bit cautious. We're buying a little. We're waiting for some more normalcy in the currency market," a foreign bank trader said.
Traders said they were not keen on bidding aggressively for the auction of the short-term, cash management bills later today.
Indications in the market are that the 35-day and 42-day bills will fetch rates of 13/14 percent which would just be in line with the special savings accounts being offered by banks to clients.
"If it falls too low, it might not be that competitive," a trader said. "Banks may shy away from them."
The Bureau of Treasury will sell a total of one billion pesos worth of these bills.
The average interbank call loan rate remained at 18.0625 percent, with volume slightly down at 18.24 billion pesos from 18.84 billion.
Out of the 49 participating financial institutions, 29 were lenders.
